chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, who said:

I was delayed from the Hajj, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What has delayed you from the Hajj?' I said: 'May I be your ransom, I guaranteed a man, but he shamed me (failed to pay).' He said: 'What is it to you and the guarantees? Do you not know that they destroyed the former generations?'
Then he said: 'A people committed many sins, so they feared them and feared a severe fear, and others came and said,
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down the punishment upon them. Then the Blessed and High said: 'You feared Me and were audacious against Me.'

key_terms.خَفَرَ: To shame or fail to fulfill responsibility
key_terms.ذُنُوبُكُمْ عَلَيْنَا: Your sins are upon us (Quranic phrase)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on financial guarantees (kafalah) and their spiritual consequences according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) critiques the narrator's delay in Hajj due to *kafalah* (financial guarantee), linking it to the Quranic narrative of the Banu Israel where they declared 'Our sin is upon you' (Surah Al-A'raf 7:168), resulting in divine punishment. This illustrates the principle of vicarious liability in Shia jurisprudence, where assuming another's burden can lead to shared consequence, while also highlighting the spiritual danger of neglecting obligatory acts like Hajj for worldly guarantees.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail from Al Fazl, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary who said,

‘I was delayed about the Hajj, so Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘What is the delay with you about the Hajj?’ So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I guaranteed (money) for a man, but he shamed me (did not fulfil his responsibility)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is it to you and the guarantee? Do you not know that it has destroyed the former generations?’
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A people sinned with numerous sins, so some of them felt pity and they feared with an intense fearing, and the others came over, so they said, ‘

’. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Sent down the Punishment upon them. Then the Blessed and High Said: “You are fearing Me<sup>azwj</sup> and are being audacious (disrespectful) to Me<sup>azwj</sup>?”’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from af-Fadf ibn Shadhan all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy who has said the following:

“I once remained behind from performing al-Hajj and abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asked, ’What caused you to remain behind from performing al-Hajj ? 5 I replied, ’I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, I bailed out a person but he violated his responsibility . 5 He (the Imam) said, ‘What do you have to do with bailsman-ship? Did you not know that people of the centuries before were destroyed ? 5
He (the Imam) then said, ‘A people committed a great many sins. They then became severely afraid. Another people came to them and said, ‘Your sins are upon us .
5 Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, sent upon them suffering and He most Blessed, most High, said, ‘You were afraid of Me, then you defied Me . 555
